title: Missing RFC 4861 hop limit validation in NS handling allows off-link NDP spoofing
description:
In lichen-ipv6/src/lib.rs handle_icmpv6() (line 860), Neighbor Solicitation messages are processed without validating that ip_header.hop_limit == 255.

RFC 4861 Section 7.1.1 mandates: 'A node MUST silently discard any received Neighbor Solicitation messages that do not satisfy all of the following validity checks: The IP Hop Limit field has a value of 255, i.e., the packet could not possibly have been forwarded by a router.'

Impact: Without this check, an attacker from a different network segment can send spoofed NS messages (which would have hop_limit < 255 after being routed). This enables:
- Off-link NDP cache poisoning
- Address hijacking on the mesh
- DoS by claiming another node's address

Fix: Add validation at the start of the NEIGHBOR_SOLICITATION case:
  if ip_header.hop_limit != 255 { return Ok(None); }

Note: Echo Request does not require hop_limit=255 per RFC 4443, so that path is not affected.
close_reason: Fixed: Added RFC 4861 Section 7.1.1 hop_limit == 255 validation at line 906-910 of lichen-ipv6/src/lib.rs. Packets with hop_limit < 255 (indicating forwarding by a router) are now silently discarded, preventing off-link NDP spoofing attacks.
